celebration.title: In Conceptione Immaculata Beatæ Mariæ Virginis

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Ant. Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Ant. Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Ant. Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
content.english: Ant. Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum eius Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

content.latin: Præclára custos Vírginum,
content.english: Blest guardian of all virgin souls,

content.latin: Intácta mater Núminis,
content.english: Portal of bliss to man forgiven,

content.latin: Cæléstis aulæ iánua,
content.english: Pure Mother of Almighty God,

content.latin: Spes nostra, cæli gáudium,
content.english: Thou hope of earth and joy of heaven!

content.latin: Inter rubéta lílium,
content.english: Fair Lily found among the thorn,

content.latin: Colúmba formosíssima,
content.english: Most beauteous Dove with wings of gold,

content.latin: Virga e radíce gérminans
content.english: Rod from whose tender root upsprang

content.latin: Nostro medélam vúlneri.
content.english: That healing Flower so long foretold

content.latin: Turris dracóni impérvia,
content.english: Thou Tower against the dragon proof,

content.latin: Amíca stella náufragis,
content.english: Thou Star to stormtossed voyagers dear;

content.latin: Tuére nos a fráudibus,
content.english: Our course lies o'er a treacherous deep,

content.latin: Tuáque luce dírige.
content.english: thine be the light by which we steer.

content.latin: Erróris umbras díscute,
content.english: Scatter the mists that round us hang;

content.latin: Syrtes dolósas ámove,
content.english: Keep far the fatal shoals away;

content.latin: Fluctus tot inter, déviis
content.english: And while through darkling waves we sweep,

content.latin: Tutam reclúde sémitam.
content.english: Open a path to light and day.

content.latin: Iesu, tibi sit glória,
content.english: O Jesu, born of Virgin bright,

content.latin: Qui natus es de Vírgine,
content.english: Immortal glory be to thee;

content.latin: Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
content.english: Praise to the Father infinite

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: And Holy Ghost eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Nocturnus I
content.english: Nocturn I

segments.t: Nocturnus I

content.latin: Ant. Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, how excellent is thy Name * in all the earth, Who hast made thee a worthy tabernacle in the Virgin Mary.

segments.t: Ant.
Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [1]
content.english: Psalm 8 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 8

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

segments.t: Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Admirábile est nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast made thee a worthy tabernacle in the Virgin Mary.

segments.t: Ant.
Admirábile est nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.

content.latin: Ant. In sole pósuit * Deus tabernáculum suum.
content.english: Ant. The Lord hath set * His tabernacle in the sun.

segments.t: Ant.
In sole pósuit * Deus tabernáculum suum.

content.latin: Psalmus 18 [2]
content.english: Psalm 18 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 18

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

segments.t: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

segments.t: In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

segments.t: Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

segments.t: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

segments.t: Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In sole pósuit Deus tabernáculum suum.
content.english: Ant. The Lord hath set His tabernacle in the sun.

segments.t: Ant.
In sole pósuit Deus tabernáculum suum.

content.latin: Ant. In Conceptióne sua * accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.
content.english: Ant. Even in her Conception * did Mary receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of her salvation.

segments.t: Ant.
In Conceptióne sua * accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.

content.latin: Psalmus 23 [3]
content.english: Psalm 23 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 23

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

segments.t: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

segments.t: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

segments.t: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

segments.t: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
content.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.

content.latin: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In Conceptióne sua accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.
content.english: Ant. Even in her Conception did Mary receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of her salvation.

segments.t: Ant.
In Conceptióne sua accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.

content.latin: ℣. Deus omnípotens præcínxit me virtúte.
content.english: ℣. It is Almighty God That girdeth me with strength.

segments.t: Deus omnípotens præcínxit me virtúte.

content.latin: ℟. Et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.
content.english: ℟. And maketh my way perfect.

segments.t: Et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De libro Génesis
content.english: From the book of Genesis

content.latin: 1 Serpens erat callídior cunctis animántibus terræ quæ fécerat Dóminus Deus. Qui dixit ad mulíerem: Cur præcépit vobis Deus ut non comederétis de omni ligno paradísi?
content.english: 1 Now the serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth which the Lord God made. And he said to the woman: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?

segments.t: Serpens erat callídior cunctis animántibus terræ quæ fécerat Dóminus Deus. Qui dixit ad mulíerem: Cur præcépit vobis Deus ut non comederétis de omni ligno paradísi?

content.latin: 2 Cui respóndit múlier: De fructu lignórum, quæ sunt in paradíso, véscimur:
content.english: 2 And the woman answered him, saying: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:

segments.t: Cui respóndit múlier: De fructu lignórum, quæ sunt in paradíso, véscimur:

content.latin: 3 De fructu vero ligni quod est in médio paradísi, præcépit nobis Deus ne comederémus, et ne tangerémus illud, ne forte moriámur.
content.english: 3 But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath commanded us that we should not eat; and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.

segments.t: De fructu vero ligni quod est in médio paradísi, præcépit nobis Deus ne comederémus, et ne tangerémus illud, ne forte moriámur.

content.latin: 4 Dixit autem serpens ad mulíerem: Nequáquam morte moriémini.
content.english: 4 And the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death.

segments.t: Dixit autem serpens ad mulíerem: Nequáquam morte moriémini.

content.latin: 5 Scit enim Deus quod in quocúmque die comedéritis ex eo, aperiéntur óculi vestri, et éritis sicut dii, sciéntes bonum et malum.
content.english: 5 For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.

segments.t: Scit enim Deus quod in quocúmque die comedéritis ex eo, aperiéntur óculi vestri, et éritis sicut dii, sciéntes bonum et malum.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Per unum hóminem peccátum in hunc mundum intrávit, in quo omnes peccavérunt.
content.english: ℟. By one man sin entered into the world, in whom all have sinned.

segments.t: Per unum hóminem peccátum in hunc mundum intrávit, in quo omnes peccavérunt.

content.latin: * Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Deum.
content.english: * Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God.

content.latin: ℣. Erípuit Dóminus ánimam tuam de morte, et contra inimícum factus est protéctor tuus.
content.english: ℣. The Lord hath delivered thy soul from death, yea, the Lord was thy stay.

segments.t: Erípuit Dóminus ánimam tuam de morte, et contra inimícum factus est protéctor tuus.

content.latin: ℟. Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Deum.
content.english: ℟. Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God.

segments.t: Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Deum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 6 Vidit ígitur múlier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescéndum, et pulchrum óculis, aspectúque delectábile: et tulit de fructu illíus, et comédit: dedítque viro suo, qui comédit.
content.english: 6 And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave to her husband who did eat.

segments.t: Vidit ígitur múlier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescéndum, et pulchrum óculis, aspectúque delectábile: et tulit de fructu illíus, et comédit: dedítque viro suo, qui comédit.

content.latin: 7 Et apérti sunt óculi ambórum; cumque cognovíssent se esse nudos, consuérunt fólia ficus, et fecérunt sibi perizómata.
content.english: 7 And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons.

segments.t: Et apérti sunt óculi ambórum; cumque cognovíssent se esse nudos, consuérunt fólia ficus, et fecérunt sibi perizómata.

content.latin: 8 Et cum audíssent vocem Dómini Dei deambulántis in paradíso ad auram post merídiem, abscóndit se Adam et uxor eius a fácie Dómini Dei in médio ligni paradísi.
content.english: 8 And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God, amidst the trees of paradise.

segments.t: Et cum audíssent vocem Dómini Dei deambulántis in paradíso ad auram post merídiem, abscóndit se Adam et uxor eius a fácie Dómini Dei in médio ligni paradísi.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me:
content.english: ℟. Come unto me all ye that be desirous of me

segments.t: Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me:

content.latin: * Et narrábo vobis quanta fecit Deus ánimæ meæ.
content.english: * And I will declare what God hath done for my soul.

content.latin: ℣. Vivit Dóminus, quóniam adimplévit in me misericórdiam suam.
content.english: ℣. As the Lord liveth, by me He hath fulfilled His mercy.

segments.t: Vivit Dóminus, quóniam adimplévit in me misericórdiam suam.

content.latin: ℟. Et narrábo vobis quanta fecit Deus ánimæ meæ.
content.english: ℟. And I will declare what God hath done for my soul.

segments.t: Et narrábo vobis quanta fecit Deus ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 9 Vocavítque Dóminus Deus Adam, et dixit ei: Ubi es?
content.english: 9 And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?

segments.t: Vocavítque Dóminus Deus Adam, et dixit ei: Ubi es?

content.latin: 10 Qui ait: Vocem tuam audívi in paradíso, et tímui, eo quod nudus essem, et abscóndi me.
content.english: 10 And he said: I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.

segments.t: Qui ait: Vocem tuam audívi in paradíso, et tímui, eo quod nudus essem, et abscóndi me.

content.latin: 11 Cui dixit: Quis enim indicávit tibi quod nudus esses, nisi quod ex ligno de quo præcéperam tibi ne coméderes, comedísti?
content.english: 11 And he said to him: And who hath told thee that thou wast naked, but that thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?

segments.t: Cui dixit: Quis enim indicávit tibi quod nudus esses, nisi quod ex ligno de quo præcéperam tibi ne coméderes, comedísti?

content.latin: 12 Dixítque Adam: Múlier, quam dedísti mihi sóciam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi.
content.english: 12 And Adam said: The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

segments.t: Dixítque Adam: Múlier, quam dedísti mihi sóciam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi.

content.latin: 13 Et dixit Dóminus Deus ad mulíerem: Quare hoc fecísti? Quæ respóndit: Serpens decépit me, et comédi.
content.english: 13 And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.

segments.t: Et dixit Dóminus Deus ad mulíerem: Quare hoc fecísti? Quæ respóndit: Serpens decépit me, et comédi.

content.latin: 14 Et ait Dóminus Deus ad serpéntem: Quia fecísti hoc, maledíctus es inter ómnia animántia, et béstias terræ: super pectus tuum gradiéris, et terram cómedes cunctis diébus vitæ tuæ.
content.english: 14 And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because thou hast done this thing, thou art cursed among all cattle, and the beasts of the earth: upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.

segments.t: Et ait Dóminus Deus ad serpéntem: Quia fecísti hoc, maledíctus es inter ómnia animántia, et béstias terræ: super pectus tuum gradiéris, et terram cómedes cunctis diébus vitæ tuæ.

content.latin: 15 Inimicítias ponam inter te et mulíerem, et semen tuum et semen illíus: ipsa cónteret caput tuum, et tu insidiáberis calcáneo eius.
content.english: 15 I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.

segments.t: Inimicítias ponam inter te et mulíerem, et semen tuum et semen illíus: ipsa cónteret caput tuum, et tu insidiáberis calcáneo eius.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Elécta mea cándida sicut nix in Líbano; sicut favus distíllans lábia eius:
content.english: ℟. My beloved is white like snow in Lebanon, her lips drop as the honeycomb.

segments.t: Elécta mea cándida sicut nix in Líbano; sicut favus distíllans lábia eius:

content.latin: * Mel et lac sub lingua illíus.
content.english: * Honey and milk are under her tongue.

content.latin: ℣. Veni de Líbano, sponsa mea, veni, coronáberis coróna gratiárum.
content.english: ℣. Come from Lebanon, My Spouse, thou shalt be crowned with a crown of grace.

segments.t: Veni de Líbano, sponsa mea, veni, coronáberis coróna gratiárum.

content.latin: ℟. Mel et lac sub lingua illíus.
content.english: ℟. Honey and milk are under her tongue.

segments.t: Mel et lac sub lingua illíus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Mel et lac sub lingua illíus.
content.english: ℟. Honey and milk are under her tongue.

segments.t: Mel et lac sub lingua illíus.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Diffúsa est * grátia in Conceptióne eius, et speciósa appáruit inter fílias hóminum.
content.english: Ant. Grace is poured into her Conception, * and she is fairer than the daughters of men.

segments.t: Ant.
Diffúsa est * grátia in Conceptióne eius, et speciósa appáruit inter fílias hóminum.

content.latin: Psalmus 44 [4]
content.english: Psalm 44 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: Qualis et quanta esset beáta et gloriósa semper Virgo María, ab Angelo divínitus declarátur, cum dícitur: Ave, grátia plena; Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus. Tálibus namque decébat Vírginem oppignorári munéribus, ut esset grátia plena, quæ dedit cælis glóriam, terris Dóminum, pacémque refúdit, fidem géntibus, finem vítiis, vitæ órdinem, móribus disciplínam. Et bene plena, quia céteris per partes præstátur; Maríæ vero simul se tota infúdit plenitúdo grátiæ. Vere plena, quia etsi in sanctis Pátribus et Prophétis grátia fuísse créditur, non tamen eátenus plena; in Maríam vero totíus grátiæ, quæ in Christo est, plenitúdo venit, quamquam áliter. Et ídeo inquit: Benedícta tu in muliéribus; id est plus benedícta quam omnes mulíeres. Ac per hoc quidquid maledictiónis infúsum est per Hevam, totum ábstulit benedíctio Maríæ. De ipsa Sálomon in Cánticis, quasi in laudem eius, Veni, inquit, colúmba mea, immaculáta mea. Iam enim hiems tránsiit, imber ábiit et recéssit. Ac deínde inquit: Veni de Líbano, veni, coronáberis.
content.english: Who and what was the blessed and glorious Mary, always a Virgin, hath been revealed by God by the message of an Angel, in these words: Hail, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee blessed art thou among women. It was fitting that a fullness of grace should be poured into that Virgin who hath given to God glory and to man a Saviour, who hath brought peace to earth, who hath given faith to the Gentiles, who hath killed sin, who hath given law to life, who hath made the crooked ways straight. Verily, she is full of grace. To others grace cometh measure by measure; in Mary grace dwelleth at once in all fullness. Verily, she is full of grace. We believe that the holy Fathers and Prophets had grace; but they were not full of grace. But into Mary came a fullness of all the grace which is in Christ, albeit otherwise than as it is in Him. Therefore is it said: Blessed art thou among women, that is, Blessed art thou above all women. The fulness of blessing in Mary utterly neutralized in her any effects of the curse of Eve. In her praise Solomon writeth in the Song of Songs, ii. 10,: Rise up, my dove, my fair one, for the winter is past, the rain is over and gone. And again: Come from Lebanon, my Spouse, come, thou shalt be crowned. ~iv. 8.

content.latin: Non immérito ígitur veníre de Líbano iubétur, quia Líbanus candidátio interpretátur. Erat enim candidáta multis meritórum virtútibus, et dealbáta nive candídior, Spíritus Sancti munéribus, simplicitátem colúmbæ in ómnibus repræséntans: quóniam, quidquid in ea gestum est, totum púritas et simplícitas, totum véritas et grátia fuit; totum misericórdia et iustítia, quæ de cælo prospéxit: et ídeo immaculáta, quia in nullo corrúpta. Circúmdedit enim virum in útero, sicut Ieremías sanctus testátur, et non aliúnde accépit. Fáciet, inquit, Dóminus novum super terram, et múlier circúmdabit virum. Vere novum, et ómnium novitátum superéminens nóvitas virtútum, quando Deus (quem ferre non potest mundus, neque vidére áliquis, ut vívere possit) sic ingréssus est hospítium ventris, ut córporis claustrum nescíret; sicque gestátus, ut totus Deus in eo esset; et sic exívit inde, ut esset (sicut Ezéchiel fatétur) porta omníno clausa. Unde cánitur in eísdem Cánticis de ea: Hortus conclúsus, fons signátus, emissiónes tuæ paradísus. Vere hortus deliciárum, in quo cónsita sunt univérsa florum génera, et odoraménta virtútum; sicque conclúsus, ut nésciat violári, neque corrúmpi ullis insidiárum fráudibus. Fons ítaque signátus sigíllo totíus Trinitátis.
content.english: Not unjustly then is she bidden to come from Lebanon, for Lebanon is so named on account of its stainless and glistening whiteness. The earthly Lebanon is white with snow, but the lonely heights of Mary's holiness are white with purity and grace, brilliantly fair, whiter far than snow, sparkling with the gifts of the Holy Ghost she is undefiled like a dove, all clean, all upright, full of grace and truth. She is full of mercy, and of the righteousness that hath looked down from heaven, and therefore is she without stain because in her hath never been any corruption. She hath compassed a man in her womb, saith holy Jeremiah, but she conceived not by the will of fallen man. The Lord, saith the Prophet, hath created a new thing in the earth; a woman shall compass a man. xxxi. 22. Verily, it is a new thing. Verily, it was a new work of power, greater than all other works, when God, Whom the world cannot bear, and Whom no man shall see and live, entered the lodging of her womb, breaking not the blissful cloister of her virgin flesh. And in her body He was borne, the Infinite inclosed within her womb. And from her womb He came forth, so that it was fulfilled which was spoken of the Prophet Ezekiel, saying: This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut. xliv. 2. Hence also in the Song of Songs it is said of her iv. 12,: A garden enclosed is my sister, my spouse, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed, thy perfumes are a garden of delights. Verily a garden of delights, filled with the perfumes of all flowers, rich with the sweet savour of grace. And the most holy Virgin herself is a garden enclosed, whereinto sin and Satan have never entered to sully the blossoms, a fountain sealed, sealed with the seal of the Trinity.

content.latin: Ex Actis Pii Papæ noni
content.english: From the acts of Pope Pius IX

content.latin: Deíparæ autem Vírginis in sua Conceptióne de tetérrimo humáni géneris hoste victóriam, quam divína elóquia, veneránda tradítio, perpétuus Ecclésiæ sensus, singuláris episcopórum ac fidélium conspirátio, insígnia quoque summórum Pontíficum acta atque constitutiónes mirífice iam illustrábant, Pius nonus Póntifex máximus totíus Ecclésiæ votis ánnuens státuit suprémo suo atque infallíbili oráculo solémniter proclamáre. Itaque sexto idus decémbris anni millésimi octingentésimi quinquagésimi quarti in basílica Vaticána, ingénti sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ patrum cardinálium et Episcopórum ex díssitis étiam regiónibus astánte cœtu, universóque plaudénte orbe, solémniter pronuntiávit et definívit: Doctrínam quæ tenet beatíssimam Vírginem Maríam in primo instánti suæ Conceptiónis fuísse, singulári Dei privilégio, ab omni originális culpæ labe præservátam immúnem, esse a Deo revelátam, ac proínde ab ómnibus fidélibus fírmiter constantérque credéndam.
content.english: The fact that the Virgin Mother of God had at the moment of her conception triumphed over the foul enemy of man, hath ever been borne out by the Holy Scriptures, by the venerable tradition of the Church, and by her unceasing belief, as well as by the common conviction of all Bishops and faithful Catholics, and by marked acts and constitutions of the Holy See. At length the Supreme Pontiff Pius IX, in compliance with the wishes of the Universal Church, determined to publish it as a truth of faith, on his own absolute and unerring authority, and accordingly, on the 8th day of December, 1854, in the Vatican Basilica, in presence of a great multitude composed of the Fathers Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, and Bishops from all parts of the earth, he, with the consent and jubilation of the whole world, declared and defined as follows That doctrine which declareth that the most Blessed Virgin Mary was in the first instant of her Conception preserved, by a special privilege granted unto her by God, from any stain of original sin, is a doctrine taught and revealed by God, and therefore is to be held by all faithful Christians firmly and constantly.

content.latin: 95:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * cantáte Dómino, omnis terra.

content.english: 95:2 Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: * shew forth his salvation from day to day.

segments.t: Cantáte Dómino, et benedícite nómini eius: * annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre eius.

content.latin: 95:3 Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam eius, * in ómnibus pópulis mirabília eius.
content.english: 95:3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles: * his wonders among all people.

content.latin: 95:4 Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.
content.english: 95:4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: * he is to be feared above all gods.

segments.t: Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.

content.latin: 95:5 Quóniam omnes dii géntium dæmónia: * Dóminus autem cælos fecit.
content.english: 95:5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: * but the Lord made the heavens.

content.english: 95:6 Praise and beauty are before him: * holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.

segments.t: Conféssio, et pulchritúdo in conspéctu eius: * sanctimónia et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne eius.

content.latin: 95:7 Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius.
content.english: 95:7 Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour: * bring to the Lord glory unto his name.

segments.t: Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius.

content.english: 95:8 Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

content.english: 95:9 Let all the earth be moved at his presence. * Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned.

content.english: 95:10 For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: * he will judge the people with justice.

segments.t: Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra: commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo eius: * gaudébunt campi, et ómnia quæ in eis sunt.

content.latin: In illo témpore: Missus est Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Ioseph, de domo David, et nomen Vírginis María. Et réliqua.
content.english: In that time, the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And so on.

content.english: Homily by St. Germain, Patriarch of Constantinople.

content.latin: In Præsentatione Deiparæ
content.english: On the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin

segments.t: In Præsentatione Deiparæ

content.latin: Ave, María, grátia plena, Sanctis sánctior, et cælis excélsior, et Chérubim gloriósior, et Séraphim honorabílior, et super omnem creatúram venerabílior. Ave, colúmba, quæ nobis et fructum fers olívæ, et servatórem a spiritáli dilúvio ac portum salútis annúntias; cuius pennæ deargentátæ, et posterióra dorsi in pallóre auri sanctíssimi et illuminántis Spíritus fulgóre irradiántur. Ave, amœníssimus et rationális Dei paradísus, benevolentíssima et omnipoténti eiúsdem dextra hódie ad Oriéntem plantátus, et ipsi suáve olens lílium, et rosam immarcescíbilem gérminans in eórum medélam, qui pestíferam animǽque exitiálem amaritúdinem mortis ad Occidéntem ebíberant; paradísus, in quo ad veritátis agnitiónem lignum vivíficum effloréscit, e quo qui gustáverint, immortalitátem consequúntur. Ave, sacrosáncte ædificátum, immaculátum, purissimúmque Dei summi Regis palátium, eiúsdem Dei Regis magnificéntia circumornátum, omnésque hospítio recípiens ac mýsticis refíciens delíciis; in quo non manufáctus et vário decóre nitens situs est spirituális Sponsi thálamus; in quo Verbum errántem humánam stirpem revocáre volens, carnem sibi desponsávit, ut eos, qui voluntáte própria extórres facti fúerant, Patri reconciliáret.
content.english: Hail, Mary, full of grace, holier than the Saints, higher than the heavens, more glorious than the Cherubim, more honourable than the Seraphim, and the most worshipful thing that the hands of God have made. Hail, O dove, bearing in thy beak the olive-branch of peace that telleth us of salvation from the spiritual flood, Gen. viii. 10, n, dove, blessed omen of a safe harbour, whose wings are of silver, and thy feathers of gold, shining in the bright beams of the Most Holy and Light-giving Spirit. Ps. lxvii. 14. Hail, thou living garden of Eden, planted towards the East by the right hand of the Most Merciful and Mighty God, wherein do grow to His glory rich lilies and unfading roses, for the healing of them that have drunk in death from the blighting and pestilential breezes of the bitter West, Gen. ii. 8, 9; Eden, wherein hath sprung that Tree of life, Whereof if any man eat he shall live for ever. Gen. ii. 9; iii. 22. John vi. 52. Hail, stately Palace of the King, most holy, stainless, purest, House of the Most High God, adorned with His Royal splendour, open to all, filled with Kingly dainties; Palace wherein is that spiritual bridal chamber, not made with hands, nor hung with diverse colours, in the which the Eternal Word, when He would raise up fallen man, wedded flesh unto Himself, that He might reconcile unto the Father them who had cast themselves away.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: * Emissiónes tuæ paradísus, o María.
content.english: * O Mary, thy perfumes are a garden of delights.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipsa Virgo vírginum intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. She whose feast-day we are keeping, Mary, blessed Maid of Maidens, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Ave, Dei mons præpínguis et umbrósus, in quo enutrítus Agnus rationális peccáta atque infirmitátes nostras portávit: mons, e quo devolútus ille nulla manu præcísus lapis, contrívit aras idolórum, et factus est in caput ánguli, mirábilis in óculis nostris. Ave, sanctus Dei thronus, divínum donárium, domus glóriæ, perpúlchrum ornaméntum, cimélium eléctum, et totíus orbis propitiatórium, cælúmque Dei glóriam enárrans. Ave, urna ex puro auro confláta, et suavíssimam animárum nostrárum dulcédinem, Christum scílicet qui manna est, cóntinens. O puríssima et omni laude et obséquio digníssima Virgo, Deo dicátum donárium omni creaturárum conditióni præcéllens, terra non secta, inarátus ager, vitis floridíssima, fons aquas effúndens, virgo génerans, et mater viri néscia, innocéntiæ thesáurus abscónditus, et sanctimóniæ decus; acceptíssimis tuis ac matérna auctoritáte válidis précibus ad Dóminum ac Deum ómnium Conditórem, Fílium tuum ex te sine patre génitum, ecclesiástici órdinis gubernácula fac dírigas, et ad portum tranquíllum perdúcas.
content.english: Hail, O rich and shady Mountain of God, whereon pastured the True Lamb, Who hath taken away our sins and infirmities, Hab. iii. 3; Isa. liii. 4; John i. 29, mountain, whereout hath been cut without hands that Stone which hath smitten the altars of the idols, and become the head-stone of the corner, marvellous in our eyes. Dan. ii. 34; Ps. cxvii. 22, 23. Hail, thou holy Throne of God, thou divinest store-house, thou temple of glory, thou bright crown, thou chosen treasure, thou mercy-seat for the whole world, thou heaven declaring the glory of God. Ps. xviii. 2. Hail, thou vessel of pure gold, made to hold the manna that came down from heaven, the sweet food of our souls, even Christ. Ex. xvi.33; Heb. ix. 4; John vi. 49-51. Hail, O purest Virgin, most praiseworthy and most worshipful, hallowed treasury for the wants of all creatures; thou art the untitled earth, the unploughed field; thou art the vine full of flowers, the well overflowing with waters, Maiden and Mother; thou art the Mother that knew not a man, the hidden treasure of guilelessness, and the clear, bright star of holiness; by thy most acceptable prayers, strong from thy motherly mouth, obtain for all estates of men in the Church that they may continually tend unto Him Who is the Lord, and God, and Maker of thee, and of them, and of all, but of thee the Son also, conceived without man's intervention; obtain this, O Mother, pilot them to the harbour of peace.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum:
content.english: ℟. My soul doth magnify the Lord;

content.english: * For He That is mighty hath done to me great things, and holy is His name.

content.latin: ℣. Ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.
content.english: ℣. For, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.

segments.t: Ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.

content.latin: ℟. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen eius.
content.english: ℟. For He That is mighty hath done to me great things, and holy is His name.

segments.t: Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen eius.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen eius.
content.english: ℟. For He That is mighty hath done to me great things, and holy is His name.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
content.english: Benediction. May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Sacerdótes iustítia, et probátæ, immaculátæ ac sincéræ fídei exsultatióne splendidíssime indúito. Orthodóxis princípibus, qui præ omni púrpuræ aut auri splendóre, et præ margarítis ac lapídibus pretiósis, te nacti sunt diadéma et induméntum ac firmíssimum regni sui ornaméntum, in tranquíllo ac próspero statu sceptra dírige. Male fidas natiónes in te ac Deum ex te génitum blasphemántes, eórum pédibus sternens subícito; subiectúmque pópulum, ut secúndum Dei præcéptum in suávi obediéntiæ obséquio persevéret, confirmáto. Tuam hanc civitátem, quæ te tamquam turrim ac fundaméntum habet, victóriæ triúmphis coronáto, et fortitúdine circumcíngens custódito Dei habitatiónem, templi decórem semper conserváto; laudatóres tuos ab omni discrímine et ánimi angóre éxime; captívis redemptiónem tribúito; peregrínis tecto et quovis præsídio destitútis, solámen te éxhibe. Univérso mundo auxiliatrícem manum tuam pórrige, ut in lætítia et exsultatióne solemnitátes tuas simul cum ista, quam modo celebrámus, festivitáte splendidissímo éxitu transigámus, in Christo Iesu universórum Rege ac vero Deo nostro, cui glória et fortitúdo una cum sancto vitǽque princípio Patre, et coætérno et consubstantiáli et conregnánte Spíritu, nunc et semper et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: Be it thine to clothe God's priests with righteousness, and to make them shout aloud for joy Ps. cxxxi. 9, 16, in approved and stainless, and upright and glorious faith. thine be it to guide in peace the sceptres of orthodox princes, even of princes who put their trust in thee to be the crown of their Majesty, and the Royal Robe of their greatness, and the firm foundation of their dominion, more than in purple, or fine gold, or pearls, or precious stones; thine be it to put under their feet the unfaithful nations, nations that blaspheme thee, and the God That was born of thee; thine be it to keep in meek obedience the people that are under them, according to the commandment of God. Behold, this is thine own city, which hath thee for her towers and her foundations, crown her with victory, gird the house of God with strength, keep undefiled the loveliness of His tabernacles, as for them that praise thy name, be thou their deliverer from strife and bitterness of spirit. Free thou the prisoner, protect the wanderer, and if there be any that hath no refuge, be thou to him a consolation. Stretch forth thine hand and help the whole earth so shall we year by year keep this and all thy feasts, and at last be found with thee in Christ Jesus, Who is Lord of all, and verily our God. To Him, with the Holy Father, Who is the Fountain of Life, and the coeternal Spirit, Three Persons and One Substance, even as there is one Kingdom, be glory and strength, now and for ever. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Te Deum
content.english: Te Deum

segments.t: Te Deum

content.latin: Te Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
content.english: We praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.

content.latin: Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
content.english: All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.

content.latin: Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
content.english: To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.

content.latin: Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
content.english: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
content.english: bow head Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;

segments.t: Fit reverentia
Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.

content.latin: Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.

content.latin: Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
content.english: The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
content.english: The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
content.english: The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.

content.latin: Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
content.english: The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;

content.latin: Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
content.english: The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.

content.latin: Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
content.english: Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;

content.latin: Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
content.english: Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.

content.latin: Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
content.english: Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.

content.latin: Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
content.english: Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

segments.t: Fit reverentia
Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

segments.t: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus
Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

segments.t: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem
Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui per immaculátam Vírginis Conceptiónem dignum Fílio tuo habitáculum præparásti: quǽsumus; ut qui ex morte eiúsdem Fílii tui prævísa, eam ab omni labe præservásti, nos quoque mundos eius intercessióne ad te perveníre concédas.
content.english: O God, by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin, thou prepared a worthy habitation for thy Son; we beseech thee, that, as by the foreseen death of thy same Son thou preserved her from all stain of sin, so thou would grant us also, through her intercession, to come to thee with pure hearts.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Tota pulchra * es, María, et mácula originális non est in te.
content.english: Ant. Thou art all fair, O Mary, * there is no spot of original sin in thee.

Tota pulchra * es, María, et mácula originális non est in te.

content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

segments.t: Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.

content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

segments.t: Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.

content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

segments.t: Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.

content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

segments.t: Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.

content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.

content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Vestiméntum tuum cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.
content.english: Ant. Thy raiment is white as snow, and thy countenance as the sun.

segments.t: Ant.
Vestiméntum tuum cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.

content.english: Ant. Thou art the exaltation of Jerusalem, * thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation.

segments.t: Ant.
Tu glória Ierúsalem, * tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
